the social networks are evolving in time, that the evolution of a network depends on its architecture, that the architecture of a network depends of the context in which it is embedded, and that the social networks have a crucial role in the evolution of health and diseases.

the evolution of social networks in a biological and age-dependent context, and with the effect of social transmission of habits on obesity, type II diabetes and neuro-degenerative diseases, and with the evolution of these diseases in a biological context.

obesity and its related diseases are the consequence of an evolution of social networks.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the social transmission of habits and the evolution of social networks are important determinants of obesity and of its consequences, type II diabetes and neuro-degenerative diseases.

the social transmission of unhealthy habits and behaviors, in a social and biologic age-dependent context, is a major factor of obesity, and accordingly of type II diabetes, and of its complications: the neurodegenerations, the Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, Huntington’s, etc., diseases.

social network’s dynamics is a major factor in the obesity epidemic.
